title: Lee Roy Selmon and the Selmon Brothers of Eufaula, Oklahoma
question: Which three Selmon brothers played football at Oklahoma?
answer: Lucious, Dewey and Lee Roy Selmon, all from Eufaula, Oklahoma, played for the Sooners. Lee Roy, the youngest, won the Outland Trophy and Lombardi Award in 1975 and reached the Pro Football Hall of Fame.
summary: Lucious, Dewey and Lee Roy Selmon of Eufaula all starred at OU. Lee Roy won the 1975 Outland and Lombardi and became the first player Tampa Bay ever drafted.
body: Few families have meant more to Oklahoma football than the Selmons of Eufaula. Three brothers, Lucious, Dewey and Lee Roy, all suited up for the Sooners, and Lee Roy was a cornerstone of OU's 1974 and 1975 national championship teams.

Lee Roy, the youngest of the three, became the most decorated. He was a consensus All-American in both 1974 and 1975, and as a senior he swept the Outland Trophy and the Lombardi Award as the nation's top lineman.

The brothers' story continued in the NFL. The expansion Tampa Bay Buccaneers made Lee Roy the first overall pick in 1976, the first draft choice in franchise history, and took Dewey in the second round, so the two lined up together on Tampa Bay's very first team. Lee Roy was named NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 1979, the season the young Bucs reached the NFC Championship Game. He made six straight Pro Bowls, covering the 1979 through 1984 seasons, before a back injury ended his career.
His honors piled up: the College Football Hall of Fame in 1988, the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1995 and the Oklahoma Hall of Fame in 2009.

Selmon's influence in Tampa reached well beyond the field. He worked in athletics at the University of South Florida, serving as athletic director from 2001 to 2004, and lent his name to a local restaurant chain. Tampa's Lee Roy Selmon Expressway is named in his honor. He died in 2011 at age 56, still one of the most respected figures ever to come out of Norman.
